topics.label: Introduction to the lecture on complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the lecturer's opening remarks and sets expectations regarding the complexity and importance of the complement system.

topics.label: Foundational framework and core mechanics of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the general organization, nomenclature rules, and pivotal molecular role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Recognition and activation pathways of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct upstream pathways that recognize pathogens and drive C3 deposition on target surfaces.

topics.label: Downstream effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the processes through which activated complement destroys pathogens and enhances immune clearance.

topics.label: Host cell regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and inhibitory mechanisms that protect host tissues from accidental complement attack.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic discusses the distinct clinical presentations and disease vulnerabilities caused by deficiencies in specific complement proteins.

topics.label: Pathogen strategies for complement evasion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the molecular mechanisms evolved by pathogens to evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Closing framing and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with final remarks and frames the upcoming topic in the lecture series.
